chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: Learning to read from Joe Hooven and alternating with Pollack
summary: Hooven marks fingerings under the notes; Davison says the band was an education, and the band alternated monthly with Pollack's.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And, uh, about in the summertime, two-thirds of the time, everything went outside --

Everything went outside unless, of course, it was raining or something - now, in the meantime, you know, Joe is teaching me how to read -- I mean a little more and a little more -- that's the slow way to learn---
You were resisting it every step of the way I think---
Well, in a way -- I was always lazy.
Well, what you like - you'd say play it so you could hear it and, then, that's all you had to do ---

Well, it was more than that--- I wanted to learn too -- and little by little -- you know, he did the hardest thing in a way -- he marked the fingering under the notes -- second valve - one, three - one, two, number three, number one---
You never really did adjust to that though - did you -- I mean, you used your own system of fingering even today --- you're still doing that---
Oh, I cross fingers some -- but that's when you learn to play by ear that you learn to do things the wrong way.
And, by cross finger you mean---

Well, meaning the same notes --- I can get the same notes open and one, two -- one, three is the same note -- I can do that. But, anyway, being with that band was a hell of an education for me. And, then, how this happened -- we'd go out say -- say we'd work the job for a month -- then we'd go out and, uh, Eddie would get us a ballroom to play in or---
And, then, Ben Pollack would come back in - right?
Then, Ben Pollack would come back for a month--- and we alternated for sometime that way.
And, your band played other places-- what other jobs you could get ---
Yes - we always had something going and sometimes it would be a little tough in spots. We'd do some one-nighters around Chicago.
you took some jobs on your own -- didn't you?
Oh, if I got a jobbing date - and I wasn't working - naturally, this I could do today---
